description: Composer 669 1.3 by Tran of Renaissance, the eight-channel DOS tracker the 669 module format was made for, running in your browser.
about: Composer 669 is a music tracker for MS-DOS by Tran (Tomasz Pytel) of Renaissance, a New York group: it mixes eight channels of samples on a Sound Blaster, in stereo on a Sound Blaster Pro, and saves its songs as .669 files. This is version 1.3, from December 1992, which Renaissance released as freeware.

It comes with no song. Bring in a .669 with the Files button; then F11 lists the songs, Enter loads one, F5 plays it and Alt+F5 follows it through its patterns. F12 saves the song, and Alt+X, then Y, quits to DOS.
What you save in it stays in this browser: the Files button can download it, bring in modules of your own, or start over.
terms: Freeware: “we are forced to release Composer 669 as freeware” and “use it as you wish, no strings attached.” (FREEWARE.TXT)
accuracy: It runs on a Sound Blaster Pro 2, without EMS, XMS or UMB: with the extended memory DOSBox gives it by default it stops at once, and on a Sound Blaster 16 it plays almost silently.
Mono: js-dos mixes the two channels into one.
Its arrow keys arrive as the keypad's, which change the instrument and the volume.

Browsers and systems may keep F11 and F12, which list and save its songs, for themselves: DosKit's on-screen keyboard has both. On Windows, Alt+F4 and Ctrl+F4, which edit and clear its song message, close the window or the tab: DosKit asks before the page closes.
imageAlt: Composer 669's pattern editor, running in DosKit
